differences.title: 1. STANDARD SUPPORT
differences.leftDesc: Leverages native browser APIs for custom elements, shadow DOM, and HTML templates without external dependencies, offering universal compatibility.
differences.rightDesc: Provides polyfills and a streamlined API over native Web Components, enhancing developer experience and enabling advanced features like reactive data binding.

differences.title: 2. REACTIVITY
differences.leftDesc: Requires manual DOM manipulation or attribute setting to reflect state changes, making complex UI updates more verbose and error-prone.
differences.rightDesc: Offers declarative, reactive data binding. Changes to properties automatically trigger component re-renders, simplifying state management and UI synchronization.

differences.title: 3. DEVELOPMENT EASE
differences.leftDesc: Defining custom elements and their lifecycle involves more explicit code, especially for managing internal state and DOM updates.
differences.rightDesc: Aims to reduce boilerplate code through a concise API, decorators, and efficient rendering, allowing developers to focus on component logic.

differences.title: 4. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Native implementation can be very performant, but manual updates might introduce inefficiencies if not optimized carefully by the developer.
differences.rightDesc: Built with performance in mind, optimizing DOM updates and efficiently managing element lifecycles for a smooth user experience.

differences.title: 5. INTEROPERABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Pure Web Components work seamlessly with any framework or no framework, as they are a browser standard and don't impose external constraints.
differences.rightDesc: Designed to work well with existing frameworks like React, Vue, and Angular, while also offering a standalone development experience.

differences.title: 6. TEMPLATING
differences.leftDesc: Uses native `<template>` elements and imperative DOM manipulation for rendering, which can be less expressive for dynamic UIs.
differences.rightDesc: Employs tagged template literals (lit-html) for declarative, efficient DOM updates, enabling reactive rendering with minimal overhead.

differences.title: 7. ECOSYSTEM & TOOLING
differences.leftDesc: Relies on browser tooling and standards; ecosystem is decentralized and driven by individual component creators and framework integrations.
differences.rightDesc: Benefits from a dedicated ecosystem including CLI tools, state management patterns, and community support specifically for Lit-based development.
